description: Electron app with aggressive native-OS integration — file dialogs, notifications, custom protocols, deep links, auto-updater, Touch Bar / JumpList, platform menus.

defaults.headline: Starter Foundry Native Desktop
defaults.subheadline: An Electron shell wired deep into the host OS — dialogs, protocols, deep links, notifications, and auto-update.

buildHints.whenToUse: Pick electron-native-os when the app is a first-class citizen of the host OS — it registers a custom `app://` protocol, handles `myapp://` deep links from the browser, opens native file dialogs, fires rich OS notifications, shows a Touch Bar on macOS and JumpList on Windows, and auto-updates via electron-updater. If the user just needs a generic Electron renderer, use electron-desktop-ts — this family pulls in more wiring than a simple renderer shell needs.
architectureNotes: src/main/index.ts is the orchestrator — it imports menu.ts / protocol.ts / deeplinks.ts / updater.ts and boots them in the right order (protocol handler MUST register before app.whenReady()).

src/main/menu.ts branches on process.platform to install the macOS app menu (with `about`, `services`, `hide`) and the Windows/Linux menu separately — macOS menus are built into the menu-bar, not the window.
src/main/protocol.ts registers `app://` for loading local assets AND declares `{{packageName}}://` in the `protocols` electron-builder block for OS-wide deep links.
src/main/deeplinks.ts handles `second-instance` (Windows/Linux single-instance lock) and `open-url` (macOS) events and forwards the URL to the renderer via IPC.
src/preload/index.ts exposes a minimal contextBridge API — NEVER enable nodeIntegration in the renderer.
Renderer is React + Vite; it talks to main only through the preload's typed bridge.
components: Native file open/save dialogs via dialog.showOpenDialog / dialog.showSaveDialog, invoked over IPC.
Rich notifications via the Notification class with actions (macOS supports reply + action buttons).
Touch Bar (macOS) — TouchBarButton + TouchBarScrubber wired to renderer commands.
JumpList (Windows) — recent documents + tasks via app.setJumpList.
Custom `app://` protocol for serving renderer assets in production (CSP-safe).
Deep-link handler (macOS open-url, Win/Linux single-instance argv sniff).
Auto-updater via electron-updater wired to GitHub Releases.
gotchas: macOS notarization: the auto-updater silently fails on unsigned / unnotarized builds. Ship with `afterSign` script calling `electron-notarize` — or users get 'app is damaged' errors.
Windows deep links: you MUST `app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient('myapp')` AND declare the protocol in electron-builder's `protocols` array, otherwise the URL scheme is registered but never routed.
Windows deep links require the single-instance lock (`app.requestSingleInstanceLock()`) — without it, clicking a `myapp://` URL launches a second copy instead of routing to the running one.
macOS `open-url` fires BEFORE `app.whenReady()` on cold launch. Cache the URL and replay after ready, otherwise deep links lose their payload on first invocation.
Custom protocol (`app://`) registered via `protocol.registerFileProtocol` must be called AFTER `app.whenReady()` but BEFORE any BrowserWindow loads — mis-order and the renderer hits 'file not found'.

Notifications require Info.plist entries on macOS (`NSUserNotificationsUsageDescription`) and a valid app identity — unsigned dev builds show 'Notification delivery failed' in console without surfacing to the user.
Auto-updater: electron-updater needs `publish` config in package.json/electron-builder.yml AND the `GH_TOKEN` env var on the CI build machine. Missing either produces silent no-op updates.
contextIsolation is ON by default in modern Electron — any renderer code that expects `window.require` will throw. Always expose via contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld.
Touch Bar and JumpList are platform-gated — guard with `process.platform === 'darwin'` / `'win32'` or you crash on the other OS.
integrations: electron-log — main-process logging that survives crashes
